Grid access-ID cache analysis; current exact-grid builder source and compiled graph.o inspected read-only. REQUIREMENTSv9.

Actual operations: first pass checks exact origin-aligned geometry then calculates cell() to obtain raw tile ID/min/max. Compiled x86-64 baseline graph.o confirms4 divisions in proof plus3 again in cell(); second-pass access lambda again performs3 divisions and per-buffer string lookup. One q48 graph has77176nonempty accesses; total actually parallel public cases158912 accesses. Each independent3-div removal eliminates231528/q48 and476736/batch dynamic div instructions; counts derived from actual declared2/3/4 regions per cholesky/trsm/madd call, not assumptions inserted into production.

Full access cache rejected: generic raw-cell+grid-index needs16B/access to avoid narrowing size_t or relying on stable vector Grid pointers. To remove second-pass empty-domain checks without revisiting regions also needs task read/write boundaries,about16B/task. q48 temporary cost1234816+313600=1548416bytes(~1.48MiB), plus at least write/read traffic and allocation. First/last/base finalized only after all geometry validated; either retain{grid,rawCell} and normalize during dependency processing, or a third rewrite pass. All first-pass existing checks and work tick counts still needed. Existing generic grow doubles capacity and conservatively retains old budget charges, potentially nearer4MiB charged unless pre-counting allocation sizes introduces another pass. Sparse/non-grid cases would allocate then discard. Optional cache failure must fall back to the original grid path (not force general builder merely because optional cache ate state/edge headroom). A size/headroom threshold cannot prove it does not crowd out future edges. This complexity and memory are not justified by measured7ms total graph time; only an unknown subset is arithmetic. Do not implement full cache.

Chosen smaller alternative authorized by root: first pass explicitly retains stride/cols quotient, offset/stride quotient and remainder, row/rows quotient, col/cols quotient while testing the same remainders. Existing implementation already must compute those quantities for exact geometry; use them to form checked tileID with add(mul(tile_row,columns),tile_col). No access arrays, no new task/metadata state, no thresholds, no changed graph edges. find_grid and geometry equality unchanged. New buffer stores already-computed columns. Second pass remains untouched. Expected save3div/nonemptyaccess in the first pass and no extra per-access memory; code roughly15lines. Actual whole-batch gain unknown; target is a subpart of measuredgraph7ms total, not7ms. Generic multi-buffer,empty,nonaligned fallback and overflow must preserve behavior. If no paired benefit, reject and close rather than extending to cache.

MINIMAL GRID DIVISION CANDIDATE IMPLEMENTED AND VALIDATED

Existing second-pass access lambda unchanged byte-for-byte at inspected addresses; compiled candidate grid body has4 static div sites versus baseline11 (new/existing branches previously duplicated cell3div each plus extra columns). Common first-pass path now4div versus7 previously, removing3div per access. No cache/allocation/retained-memory additions.
Temporary generic graph CSR, indegrees, offsets and error outputs exactly matched unchanged P010 library for exact multiple buffers,empty accesses,unaligned and mixed geometry,sparse fallback,empty graph,size overflow,seven memory budgets,six work limits. Each successfully built graph passed independent validate_graph reachability. No timing assertion.
